items.stem: ORANGE BOOK TE-CODE EVIDENCE — FDA lists Unithroid levothyroxine sodium 0.3-mg tablets with AB1, AB2 and AB3 codes. Assume hypothetical Product P (same strength/form/route) has AB1 only and hypothetical Product Q has AB2 only. What follows from the shared-code rule? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: Product P is not therapeutically equivalent to Unithroid because Unithroid has three ratings.
choices.why: Incorrect. A shared AB1 is sufficient to establish FDA therapeutic equivalence for products under the same heading, with matching equivalent product details.

choices.text: Unithroid may be FDA-rated therapeutically equivalent to both P and Q through its shared AB1 and AB2 codes.
choices.why: Correct. The FDA preface explicitly discusses a product with multiple AB codes; one common code establishes a TE relationship to the multi-coded product.

choices.text: P and Q must be rated therapeutically equivalent to each other solely because both share a code with Unithroid.
choices.why: Incorrect. Different numbered codes alone do not establish equivalence directly between single-coded P and single-coded Q.

choices.text: Product Q may be therapeutically equivalent to Unithroid through the shared AB2 code.
choices.why: Correct. The reference product may share more than one AB code; matching AB2 supports this relationship.

items.citation: FDA Orange Book Preface §1.7 and Levothyroxine Sodium multiple-TE-code discussion (Unithroid 0.3 mg AB1, AB2, AB3)
items.novelty_rationale: Replaces D041 single AB1/AB2 matching (already C118) with a multi-coded real reference and two distinct single-code comparisons; hypothetical products P/Q only.

items.stem: An NDA holder markets a branded drug and later markets an authorized generic under that SAME approved NDA. Its regulatory team thinks no FDA reporting is necessary because a separate ANDA was not filed. What does FDA require?

choices.text: File a second ANDA before reporting the authorized generic.
choices.why: Incorrect. Authorized generics are marketed under the original approved NDA rather than a newly approved ANDA.

choices.text: Notify FDA of the authorized generic in the NDA holder's applicable annual report.
choices.why: Correct. 21 CFR 314.81(b)(2) requires authorized generic marketing details in the annual report; the FDA publishes the list.

choices.text: Report only if a pharmacist discovers a dispensing error involving the authorized generic.
choices.why: Incorrect. Authorized generic annual reporting does not depend on a medication error.

choices.text: The wholesaler, not the NDA holder, must submit the authorized-generic annual report.
choices.why: Incorrect. The responsible annual-reporting party is the NDA holder.

items.citation: 21 CFR 314.81(b)(2) (authorized generic drugs in NDA annual report); FD&C Act §505(t); FDA Authorized Generics FAQ
items.novelty_rationale: Replaces already-tested generic-without-Orange-Book-entry E30-019 with a different legal obligation: NDA holder authorized-generic annual notification to FDA.

items.stem: FDA PURPLE BOOK PRODUCT RECORD — Semglee (insulin glargine-yfgn), BLA 761201, reference Lantus. Product 001: 1,000 units/10 mL; Product 002: 300 units/3 mL. Which records correctly follow the FDA listing? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: Product 001 is an FDA-listed multidose vial under a 351(k) interchangeable license.
choices.why: Correct. The FDA Purple Book lists product 001 with 1,000 units/10 mL, multidose vial, license type 351(k) Interchangeable.

choices.text: Product 002 is a 300 units/3 mL oral tablet with non-interchangeable status.
choices.why: Incorrect. The record specifies subcutaneous injection, autoinjector, and interchangeable status.

choices.text: Product 002 is an FDA-listed 300 units/3 mL autoinjector under the same BLA.
choices.why: Correct. The FDA entry explicitly lists the 300 units/3 mL autoinjector as product 002.

choices.text: The listing names every long-acting insulin as Semglee's reference product.
choices.why: Incorrect. The listed reference product is specifically Lantus, not all basal insulins.

items.citation: FDA Purple Book product details BLA 761201, products 001 and 002; 351(k) Interchangeable with reference Lantus
items.novelty_rationale: Uses real presentation-level Purple Book product numbers, strengths and forms; unlike C119 general biosimilar distinction and D044 prescriber prohibition.

items.stem: A physician prescribes the reference biologic Lantus for one patient and writes 'no substitution' on that patient's prescription. The pharmacy stocks an FDA-designated interchangeable insulin glargine product. Which Massachusetts action is appropriate?

choices.text: Substitute because the prescriber would have to ban substitution for every future patient.
choices.why: Incorrect. The prohibition may be individual and patient-specific under §12EE(c).

choices.text: Substitute if the pharmacist first updates the interoperable EHR.
choices.why: Incorrect. EHR communication applies after a lawful substitution and cannot override an explicit written prohibition.

choices.text: A cost preference overrides the written prohibition for this patient's biologic prescription.
choices.why: Incorrect. A request alone does not remove an operative patient-specific written no-substitution instruction.

choices.text: Honor the patient-specific written prohibition; seek new authorization before a switch.
choices.why: Correct. M.G.L. c.112 §12EE(c) bars substitution if the prescriber instructs otherwise in writing for that patient.

items.novelty_rationale: Reverse-decision test: an actual written patient-specific prohibition negates otherwise allowable FDA interchangeability.

items.stem: A commercial drug repackager puts each single-dose unit into its own sealed, labeled carton. The outer carton clearly displays the legally required expiration date; the immediate small unit container does not. Under the express federal exception, how is the expiration-date location treated?

choices.text: It may appear on the individual carton instead of the immediate single-dose container.
choices.why: Correct. 21 CFR 201.17 expressly permits the date on individual cartons of single-dose containers.

choices.text: The date must appear only in the pharmacy's dispensing computer.
choices.why: Incorrect. A computer record does not substitute for federally required manufacturer/repackager labeling.

choices.text: The date may be omitted everywhere when the original manufacturer once assigned an expiration date.
choices.why: Incorrect. Repackaging does not erase the expiration-date labeling requirement.

choices.text: It must appear on both carton and small immediate container in every single-dose case.
choices.why: Incorrect. The regulation provides a specific individual-carton exception.

items.novelty_rationale: Tests FDA single-dose carton exception, not USP BUD or MA prescription label requirements.

items.stem: An outpatient collects a prescription medicine for which an FDA Medication Guide is required under 21 CFR Part 208. The pharmacist has no valid exception, and the patient requests the guide electronically instead of paper. What follows? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: The pharmacist may omit the guide because a prescription label already gives dosing instructions.
choices.why: Incorrect. A pharmacy prescription label does not replace a required FDA Medication Guide.

choices.text: Offer the current Medication Guide when dispensing the product to the patient or authorized agent.
choices.why: Correct. 21 CFR 208.24(e) requires providing the guide when a covered product is dispensed, barring an applicable exception.

choices.text: A patient may request electronic provision of the Medication Guide instead of the paper version.
choices.why: Correct. FDA patient-labeling resources expressly describe patient-requested electronic delivery.

choices.text: Every Medication Guide requirement means the medicine is part of an active REMS.
choices.why: Incorrect. FDA explains Medication Guides can be labeling requirements without a REMS.

items.novelty_rationale: Patient's electronic-format request vs delivery itself, not a general REMS eligibility exercise.

items.stem: An oral contraceptive prescription is correctly filled. A technician says the FDA's Patient Package Insert (PPI) is optional because a pharmacy-generated Rx label and counseling have already been provided. Which federal requirement still applies?

choices.text: A PPI is required only when the drug is listed in the DEA schedules.
choices.why: Incorrect. Controlled-substance scheduling is unrelated to oral-contraceptive patient-package-insert duties.

choices.text: A PPI is required only for injectable contraceptives.
choices.why: Incorrect. FDA specifically requires PPIs for oral contraceptives.

choices.text: Provide the required oral-contraceptive PPI with each dispensing.
choices.why: Correct. FDA PPIs for oral contraceptives have their own mandated distribution requirement.

choices.text: Every FDA-approved prescription drug requires a mandatory PPI under 21 CFR 310.501.
choices.why: Incorrect. The requirement is category-specific; many patient information inserts are voluntary.

items.novelty_rationale: PPI vs ordinary patient Rx label; specific oral-contraceptive rule not previously tested as direct PPI distribution.

items.stem: A COMMERCIAL FDA-registered firm repackages previously unopened solid oral medicine with 16 months remaining before manufacturer expiration. All five FDA July 2020 guidance conditions are met; no additional stability data support a longer date. What expiry window falls within the guidance's ordinary enforcement-discretion policy?

choices.text: Twelve months, half of the manufacturer's remaining shelf life.
choices.why: Incorrect. The FDA policy compares six months with 25% of remaining time, not 50%.

choices.text: Assign 24 months because the drug manufacturer approved the original expiration date.
choices.why: Incorrect. The original container's stability evidence does not automatically transfer to a different unit-dose package.

choices.text: Six months, because the original manufacturer still has over one year of remaining shelf life.
choices.why: Incorrect. FDA's ordinary guideline also compares 25% of remaining shelf life; 25% of sixteen months is four months.

choices.text: Use four months: 25% of the remaining sixteen months, shorter than six.
choices.why: Correct. Twenty-five percent of 16 months is four months, which is shorter than six; this is FDA enforcement-discretion guidance for commercial firms, not a general legal pharmacy BUD.

items.citation: FDA July 2020 Guidance, Unit-Dose Repackaged Solid Oral Dosage Form Drug Products, §III; 21 CFR 211.137, 211.166
items.novelty_rationale: Scope explicitly commercial repackager, not state-licensed pharmacy, and differentiates nonbinding policy from enforceable CGMP obligation.

items.stem: MassHealth NURSING FACILITY UNIT-DOSE RETURN LOG. Assume each drug is Appendix F-listed, intact, safe, with an adequate unused quantity, paid entirely by MassHealth; treatment was discontinued and no other exclusion applies. Which shipments qualify for the 130 CMR 456.621 return-for-credit rule? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: Drug A: discontinued 20 days ago; earliest labeled expiration is 150 days from the return date.
choices.why: Correct. Correct eligibility: the return occurs within 30 days of discontinuation and at least 90 days before expiration.

choices.text: Drug B: discontinued 18 days ago; earliest labeled expiration is 80 days from return.
choices.why: Incorrect. The regulation requires return at least 90 days before the earliest label expiration.

choices.text: Drug C: discontinued 35 days ago; earliest labeled expiration is 180 days from return.
choices.why: Incorrect. The return is beyond the 30-day deadline after discontinuation.

choices.text: Drug D: discontinued 8 days ago; earliest labeled expiration is 130 days from return.
choices.why: Correct. Both the 30-day discontinuation deadline and 90-day-before-expiration requirement are satisfied.

items.citation: 130 CMR 456.621(A)(1)-(2),(B)(1)-(4) (MassHealth nursing-facility unused unit-dose returns); Appendix F eligibility
items.novelty_rationale: Replaces 247 CMR 9.13 never-dispensed return-to-stock (already E30-089) with different 130 CMR 456.621 nursing-facility return-for-credit 30-day and 90-day limits; does not assert products may be restocked.

items.stem: A 2002 MassHealth memo cites 130 CMR 406.446 as authority for the return of unused nursing-facility unit doses. A supervisor wants to apply that old section number to a 2026 return. Which CURRENT regulation more directly establishes the MassHealth nursing facility's duty to return eligible unit-dose medicines?

choices.text: 130 CMR 406.446, which now requires prospective drug review and counseling.
choices.why: Incorrect. The current text of 406.446 deals with drug review and counseling, not the old return provision.

choices.text: 130 CMR 456.621 governs the nursing-facility returns.
choices.why: Correct. The current MassHealth Nursing Facility Manual separately governs returns of unused specified unit-dose drugs.

choices.text: 247 CMR 16.03, the community CDTM regulation.
choices.why: Incorrect. CDTM protocol eligibility does not govern the nursing facility unit-dose return program.

choices.text: 21 CFR 208.24, the federal Medication Guide distribution regulation.
choices.why: Incorrect. Medication Guide rules are a different document-delivery requirement.

items.citation: 130 CMR 456.621(A); current 130 CMR 406.446; MassHealth Nursing Facility Manual Appendix F
items.novelty_rationale: Tests material 2002→2024 renumbering/supersession, not a speculative statewide donation exception.

editorial_change: D048 initial 24-month remaining example made both 6-month distractor and correct answer numerically defensible; changed to 16-month/4-month scenario to leave a unique legal and arithmetic result.
editorial_note: Corrected duplicated legal decisions: D041 multi-code real Unithroid reference instead of C118 single-code match; D042 NDA-holder authorized generic annual report instead of E30-019; D043 actual Purple Book presentation fields, D049 nursing facility unit-dose return for credit instead of E30-089 return-to-stock.
